description: A new request path through a tunnel sends every search body chunked. The reviewer couldn't confirm the server accepts that, the PR's live check only hit a no-body endpoint, and it posted the risk as an optional hardening suggestion on an approval. A possible break of the change's main path that nothing checked blocks as needing a check, naming the check. The missing test for the new request function is a should-fix note here (tests not required), and a speculative edge-case timeout stays a note.

findings.title: Tunnelled requests with a body are sent without Content-Length
findings.body: `request` passes `init.body` as a JSON string. On the `fetch` path, Node sets `Content-Length` for a string body. On the new `https.request` path no length is set, so Node sends `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` for every search with a body: `search query`, `find-class` and the trace hop. I couldn't confirm whether the private domain accepts chunked search requests; the description's live check names `_cluster/health`, which has no body. Setting the header keeps both paths sending the same thing.

findings.title: requestViaTunnel has no test
findings.body: The new tests cover `isPrivateEndpoint` and `proxyConfig`, but nothing exercises `requestViaTunnel` or the `credentials.tunnelPort` branch in `request`. That code carries the TLS servername/Host handling and the response shape that `searchIndex` relies on. Suggested test: start a local `https.createServer` and assert the Host header, path and JSON.

findings.title: A slow bastion might time out the first connection
findings.body: If the bastion is slow to start, the first connection might time out. I couldn't confirm how long it takes; a retry would be nice to have.
